question: What is the minimum strength of the Legislative Council?
solution:
The correct answer is __**40 members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of the state legislature in some Indian states.
 
• Article 171 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of Legislative Councils.
 
• According to this article, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly ¹ of that state. 
 
• However, the Constitution also specifies a minimum strength.
 
• The minimum strength of a Legislative Council must be 40 members.
 
• This minimum ensures that the council has a reasonable size and representation.
 
• There are exceptions to this. For example, Jammu and Kashmir, before it was reorganized, had a lower number of members due to its special status.
 
• The composition of the Legislative Council includes members nominated by the Governor, elected by local authorities, elected by graduates, and elected by teachers.
 
• Members are also elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The term of a member of the Legislative Council is six years.
 
• One-third of the members retire every two years, making it a continuous chamber.
 
• The Legislative Council is not present in all states of India.
 
• Its existence depends on the decision of the state legislature and Parliament.
 
• The council acts as a revising chamber, providing a second look at legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• It is intended to provide a platform for experienced individuals and experts to contribute to legislation.
 
• The council's powers are generally less than those of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• It cannot block money bills.
 
• It can delay non-money bills, but the Assembly can override its decisions.
 
• The purpose of the Legislative Council is to provide a more deliberative and balanced approach to lawmaking.
 
• It is meant to provide a check on the potentially hasty decisions of the lower house.
 
• The Indian constitution created the ability for states to create these councils, in order to create a bi-cameral legislative system.
